chemical.name: Copper-based bactericide (Copper Hydroxide)
chemical.interval: Apply every 7-10 days under humid conditions.

organic.name: Neem oil spray (0.5%) & Bacillus subtilis bio-bactericide

preventive: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead watering to keep leaves dry.
Use certified disease-free seeds and seedlings.
best_practices: Promptly remove and destroy infected leaves.
Sanitize pruning tools with 70% alcohol between plants.
Maintain adequate plant spacing (45-60 cm) for air circulation.

chemical.name: Chlorothalonil 75% WP or Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical.interval: Apply every 7-14 days starting at first symptom.

organic.name: Bio-fungicide containing Trichoderma viride or Copper Octanoate

preventive: Mulch soil surface around plant base to prevent fungal spore splashback.
Avoid working in wet foliage to prevent spore distribution.
Select resistant tomato varieties.
best_practices: Prune lower leaves up to 30 cm from ground level.
Clear crop residues immediately after harvest.
Ensure proper nitrogen balance without excess fertilization.

chemical.name: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb
chemical.interval: Apply immediately at outbreak; repeat every 5-7 days.

organic.name: Fixed copper spray combined with organic compost tea

preventive: Avoid planting near potato fields (common host).
Provide greenhouse ventilation to keep relative humidity below 85%.
Implement strict field drainage.
best_practices: Destroy heavily infected plants immediately by burying or burning.
Monitor weather forecasts for cool, wet late-blight risk periods.
Keep canopy dry with drip lines.

organic.name: Sulfur dust/spray or Potassium Bicarbonate solution

preventive: Maximize greenhouse airflow using exhaust fans and side vents.
Keep canopy humidity low by early morning irrigation.
Space rows generously.
best_practices: Remove lower yellowing leaves promptly.
Sterilize greenhouse stakes and wire support systems.
Avoid high nitrogen application.

chemical.name: Mancozeb 75% WP or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP
chemical.interval: Apply every 7-10 days during rainy weather.

organic.name: Liquid copper soap fungicide & bio-control agents

preventive: Apply straw or plastic mulch to cover soil.
Practice strict 3-year crop rotation.
Eliminate nightshade weeds around field perimeters.
best_practices: Remove bottom 4-6 leaves as plant grows.
Avoid overhead watering.
Clean tools and boots when moving between plots.

chemical.name: Abamectin 1.9% EC or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC
chemical.interval: Apply twice with a 5-7 day gap to disrupt egg hatching cycle.

organic.name: Insecticidal soap spray, Neem oil (1%), or predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis)

preventive: Maintain optimal soil moisture to reduce dry dust conditions.
Keep field borders free of broadleaf weeds.
Spray undersides of leaves with water jet.
best_practices: Regularly inspect leaf undersides with a hand lens.
Avoid broad-spectrum chemical insecticides that kill beneficial predatory insects.
Isolate infested plants.

preventive: Maintain proper foliage aeration through pruning.
Use drip irrigation systems.
Rotate with non-host crops like corn or beans.
best_practices: Remove symptomatic lower leaves early.
Maintain balanced potassium and calcium soil nutrients.
Sanitize equipment.

chemical.name: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL or Acetamiprid 20% SP (Targeting vector whiteflies)

organic.name: Yellow sticky traps, Neem oil (1%), and Beauveria bassiana entomopathogenic fungus

preventive: Install fine insect-proof mesh netting (50-mesh) in greenhouses.
Use reflective silver mulches to repel whiteflies.
Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids.
best_practices: Routinely monitor yellow sticky traps for whitefly counts.
Remove virus-infected plants in sealed bags immediately.
Keep surrounding fields weed-free.

chemical.name: No chemical cure exists for viral infections; focus on vector control and sanitation.

organic.name: Skim milk spray (10% solution) on hands/tools during pruning to deactivate virus particles.

preventive: Use certified virus-free seeds.
Wash hands with soap and water before handling plants (especially smokers, as tobacco carries virus).
Plant mosaic-resistant varieties.
best_practices: Immediately rogue (dig up and burn) infected plants.
Disinfect pruning tools in 10% TSP or bleach between plants.
Avoid handling plants when wet.

chemical.name: No chemical treatment needed for healthy plants.

organic.name: Apply organic compost tea or seaweed extract for plant vigor.

preventive: Maintain balanced N-P-K fertilization and regular watering schedule.
Continue weekly crop monitoring.
Keep canopy well-ventilated.
best_practices: Maintain clean weed-free garden beds.
Ensure adequate sunlight (6-8 hours daily).
Keep soil mulched for moisture retention.
